findings.finding: The rate path is better for NII than FHN's own 2026 guide assumed. The guide's base case (forward curve as of 2025-10-31) assumed 25bp Fed cuts in April and July 2026. Neither happened: the Fed held at 3.50-3.75% in July and hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the September SEP median implies one more hike. FHN discloses itself as modestly asset sensitive: +2.9% next-12-month NII for +100bp, -3.3% for -100bp (58% variable-rate loans). Against the plan the gap is ~75bp of short rate, worth roughly +2% on ~$2.7B of annual NII. That supports NII and the NIM guide and could raise the FY NII/revenue view on the call.
